name: Poland (since 1918)
summary: Poland reborn in 1918 after 123 years of partition: invaded in 1939, a communist state from 1945, and a democracy since Solidarity’s victory in 1989.

knownFor.label: Solidarity
knownFor.note: Trade union movement that helped end communism.

knownFor.label: Marie Curie
knownFor.note: Born in Warsaw; first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

location.value: Central Europe between Germany and the Baltic states, Belarus and Ukraine; about 313,000 km².

terrain.value: Mostly flat plains; mountains in the south.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

climate.value: Continental in the east and temperate in the west, with cold winters and warm summers.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

resources.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

disasters.value: The great flood of 1997 hit the Oder basin, and war and occupation (1939–45) killed about six million Polish citizens.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

population.value: Over 37 million, the fifth most populous EU member.

urbanisation.value: Warsaw is the capital and largest city; others include Kraków, Wrocław, Łódź, Poznań and Gdańsk.

disease.value: Public health is good, with life expectancy rising since 1989.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

migration.value: Borders moved west in 1945; millions were expelled or resettled.

economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

moneyAndTax.value: The złoty; Poland is in the EU single market but has not adopted the euro.

inequality.value: Moderate inequality, with regional differences between east and west.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

governmentType.value: Republic (1918), communist people’s republic (1947–89), democratic republic since 1989.

keyRulers.value: Józef Piłsudski, who led the May Coup (1926). Later and present leaders are not named here.

stability.value: Devastated in the Second World War: around 6 million citizens died, the highest share of any country, including the Jews murdered in the Holocaust.

eliteConflict.value: Political polarisation between liberal and conservative camps.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

majorWars.value: Polish–Soviet War (1919–21); invaded by Germany and the USSR (1939).

alliancesRivals.value: The Visegrád Group (1991), NATO (1999) and the EU (2004).

inventions.value: Maria Skłodowska-Curie’s work in physics and chemistry, mostly done in France.

scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

openness.value: Open to Europe since 1989, and a member of the EU since 2004.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

communicationTransport.value: Railways and a growing motorway network.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

religion.value: Mostly Catholic; one of the most religious countries in Europe, where Pope John Paul II is widely revered.

languageWriting.value: Polish, written in the Latin alphabet with special letters.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

artsArchitecture.value: Film directors such as Andrzej Wajda, Roman Polański and Agnieszka Holland.

socialStructure.value: A large middle class, with regional differences.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

sharedIdentity.value: Strong national identity forged through partitions and war.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

dailyLife.value: Apartment blocks and houses; pierogi, bread, soup.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

neighbours.value: Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, Russia (Kaliningrad).

colonisation.value: None; Poland itself was partitioned and occupied.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

peakPeriod.value: Rapid growth after 1989, among the fastest in Europe.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

declineSignals.value: War and occupation, in particular the invasion of 1939, were the main blows.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

outcome.value: Poland continues as an independent republic.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

sources.value: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland

overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Poland; Wikipedia: History of Poland
